question: Perform quality control on a single-cell RNA-seq dataset to preserve high-quality cells, filtering for specific criteria such as the number of genes (200~4500), mitochondrial reads (< 10%), and UMI counts (< 40000). Report the QC metrics (cell_barcode, nFeature_RNA, nCount_RNA, mito.percent) for the filtered cells.

files.eval_guideline: The set of retained cell barcodes must exactly match the reference; numeric QC values must match within +/-1e-6; row order may differ.
files.match_reasoning: The filenames are identical (filtered_cells_qc.tsv) and both are TSV files. The candidate holds the filtered-cell QC metrics the task asks for.

parameters.question: Compare QC metric tables (cell_barcode, nFeature_RNA, nCount_RNA, mito.percent) for cells retained after filtering on 200<nFeature_RNA<4500, mito.percent<10, nCount_RNA<40000. The set of retained cell barcodes must exactly match the reference; numeric QC values must match within +/-1e-6; row order may differ.

files.strategy_reasoning: This QC filtering task is deterministic. The guideline asks for the same set of retained barcodes, numeric values within 1e-6 and allows rows in any order, so approximate (record-level, order-independent) comparison fits.

align_plan.reasoning: Both tables have the same shape and identical column names, so the columns map one-to-one and no transpose is needed. cell_barcode is a unique identifier for each cell, so rows are matched on it. The output is the set of cells that passed QC, and the guideline says row order may differ, so order doesn't matter. Permutation checking is on, and both tables are sorted by cell_barcode before comparison. The QC metric columns are computed values, so they are compared within the ±1e-6 tolerance rather than used as keys.

column_configs.name: nFeature_RNA
column_configs.reasoning: Integer count of detected genes. It is computed exactly from the matrix, so it must match exactly (near-zero RAE tolerance).

column_configs.name: nCount_RNA
column_configs.reasoning: Integer UMI count per cell. It is computed exactly, so it must match exactly.

column_configs.name: mito.percent
column_configs.reasoning: Mitochondrial fraction in the range ~0.004–0.1. The guideline's ±1e-6 absolute tolerance is about 1e-5 to 2.5e-4 relative, so an RAE tolerance of 1e-4 allows for float rounding but flags scale or gene-set differences.

comparison_plan.overall_reasoning: The task asks for QC filtering. The guideline says the retained barcodes must match the reference exactly and numeric QC values must agree within ±1e-6. Barcode set membership is handled by aligning on cell_barcode, so only the three QC metric columns are compared, and all three matter equally. nFeature_RNA and nCount_RNA are integer counts, so they are checked cell by cell with RAE and a near-zero tolerance, which in practice means an exact match. mito.percent is a fraction, roughly 0.004–0.1. An absolute tolerance of 1e-6 works out to a relative error of about 1e-5 to 2.5e-4 across that range, so an RAE tolerance of 1e-4 is used. It catches real differences, such as a 0–100 percentage scale or a different set of mitochondrial genes, while ignoring floating-point noise. Signs carry meaning here, so no absolute-value comparison is used.
